mgmt_bio.text: Dr. Lisa T. Su is AMD's Chair, President and Chief Executive Officer, having served on the board since October 2014, been named Chair in February 2022, and held the President and CEO role since October 2014. She joined AMD in January 2012 as Senior Vice President and General Manager, Global Business Units, and was Chief Operating Officer from July to October 2014. Before AMD she was Senior Vice President and General Manager, Networking and Multimedia at Freescale Semiconductor, which she joined in 2007 as Chief Technology Officer, following 13 years at IBM, including as Vice President of its Semiconductor Research and Development Center. She holds bachelor's, master's and doctorate degrees in electrical engineering from MIT, is an IEEE Fellow, and chairs the Semiconductor Industry Association board.

mgmt_recent.text: Dr Lisa T Su remains chair, president and chief executive, with no succession changes disclosed. In February 2026 AMD appointed Ariel Kelman as senior vice president and chief marketing officer, reporting to chief administrative officer Ruth Cotter, and in May 2026 named Vinay Awasthi senior vice president of sales for Asia Pacific and Japan under sales chief Darren Grasby. At board level, Tim Ryan joined in August 2026 and KC McClure became chair of the Audit and Finance Committee, following Joseph Householder's retirement. Su used her October 2026 OCP Global Summit keynote to frame AMD's strategy around open, full-stack infrastructure for agentic AI.

mgmt_team_view.text: Public sources show a long-tenured leadership team: Dr Lisa Su has been AMD's president and chief executive since October 2014 and was named chairman of the board in February 2022, so the chair and chief executive roles are combined. On strategy execution, AMD completed its roughly $49bn acquisition of Xilinx in 2022. On capital allocation, the board approved a new $6bn repurchase programme in May 2025, lifting total authority to $14bn; AMD bought back 12 million shares for $1.3bn during 2025, with $9.4bn remaining at 27 December 2025. In October 2025 AMD issued OpenAI a warrant for up to 160 million shares at $0.01, vesting in tranches tied to Instinct GPU purchase milestones and share-price targets.

thesis_pillars.text:
AMD's data center franchise is the core driver: second quarter 2026 data center revenue was $6.7 billion, up 107% year-over-year on demand for EPYC processors and Instinct GPUs, representing 58% of total revenue.
Anchor AI customers give visibility: AMD and OpenAI announced a 6 gigawatt, multi-year agreement, with the first 1 gigawatt of Instinct MI450 GPUs beginning in the second half of 2026.
Mix shift is lifting profitability: data center operating income reached $2.1 billion at a 31% operating margin, with gross margin of 56%, up over 200 basis points year-over-year.
Management guides further acceleration: third quarter 2026 revenue of about $13 billion, roughly 41% growth year-over-year at the midpoint.
